title: Good: null-byte rejection at WhoIs trust boundary
description: kith-tslocal/src/lib.rs whois() explicitly checks user_id and login_name for null bytes before returning, with clear comments explaining why (SQL prepared statements, string comparison bugs). This is the correct place to enforce this invariant — at the point where untrusted network data crosses into the application's identity namespace. A contributor might be tempted to remove these checks as 'unnecessary' because Tailscale controls the API; the checks should stay because tailscaled is on the same host but is still a separate process whose response is untrusted bytes from the wire.
